title: Teriyaki-Glazed Flank Steak
summary: Two flank steaks, soy-mirin marinade, grilled hot and brushed with the reduced marinade so the glaze sets instead of burning.

ingredients.note: two steaks; this household eats the second one

steps.title: Marinade
steps.text: Whisk the soy sauce, mirin, brown sugar, sake, garlic, ginger and sesame oil until the sugar dissolves. Pour off and refrigerate 1 cup of it for the glaze before the meat goes anywhere near it.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Put both steaks in a zip bag with the rest of the marinade, press out the air, and refrigerate 45 minutes to 4 hours. Pull them 30 minutes before grilling.

steps.title: Glaze
steps.text: Simmer the reserved cup in a small pan. Stir the cornstarch into 1 tablespoon of water, whisk it in, and cook until it coats a spoon, about 3 minutes. Keep warm.

steps.title: Grill
steps.text: Two zones, hot side ripping. Pat the steaks mostly dry and sear 4 to 5 minutes per side for medium-rare, 125 to 130°F. Sugar in the marinade means the outside will darken fast; move to the cool side if it blackens before the center is there.

steps.title: Brush and rest
steps.text: In the last minute, brush both sides with the glaze. Rest 10 minutes on a board.

steps.title: Slice
steps.text: Slice thin against the grain. Spoon more glaze over the slices and finish with scallions and sesame seeds.

notes: Reconstructed from memory of the meal; not yet re-cooked from this write-up. The plate is sweet and rich, so the sides carry the acid, salt and heat: miso mash, chili crisp broccoli, wasabi crema on the side. Serves is a real family batch, not a nominal four.
